generic: Write as a native speaker would for a modern consumer app: natural, idiomatic, never calqued. Register: use the informal address if modern youth-oriented app copy in this language uses it, but keep the polite/formal form if this language stays formal in app copy regardless of audience age — get the modern feel from fresh, light phrasing, not forced slang.

locales.ar: Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), not a regional dialect. Address the reader in the generic masculine, and get a warm, contemporary feel through fresh, light phrasing. Right-to-left: keep punctuation and any Latin tokens (e.g. "iCloud") correctly placed for RTL.
locales.bn: Conversational Bengali (Bangla) in Bengali script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.ca: Natural, friendly Catalan as used in Apple's Catalan UI; warmth comes from clear, unfussy phrasing, not slang.
locales.cs: Vykání: second-person plural verb forms, lowercase "vy/váš". Warmth comes from modern, natural phrasing over literal calques, not from tykání; avoid stiff officialese.
locales.de: Keep it respectful: warm and direct, never chummy or slangy; avoid stiff officialese and English calques. German typically runs longer than English — keep compounds tight so labels don't overflow.
locales.el: Plural verb forms and "σας". Warmth comes from modern, everyday Greek; avoid overly formal or bureaucratic phrasing.
locales.en-AU: Australian English spelling and idiom (e.g. "organise", "colour"). Relaxed, friendly tone.
locales.es: Castilian Spanish (not "vosotros" for a single reader). Spain vocabulary (e.g. "móvil"). Modern and relaxed, never slangy.
locales.es-MX: Latin American Spanish; keep it courteous, never slangy. Neutral LatAm vocabulary (e.g. "celular"); avoid Spain-specific terms.
locales.fi: Sinä forms, mostly implicit in the verb, e.g. "Lisää". Direct, natural Finnish app tone, not literal. Finnish runs long — keep UI labels tight.
locales.fr: Warmth comes from clear, light, unfussy phrasing, never stiff administrative French. Elegant and concise; prefer natural French terms over anglicisms. French app copy prizes clarté and a refined, slightly understated register over an enthusiastic one.
locales.fr-CA: Canadian French. Warmth comes from plain, friendly phrasing, not tutoiement. Prefer Québécois usage and OQLF-style avoidance of anglicisms where they differ from France French.
locales.gu: Conversational Gujarati in Gujarati script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.he: Modern Hebrew. Avoid gendered second-person forms: use infinitives for actions (e.g. "להוסיף") and noun phrases for labels, and where direct address is unavoidable use plural imperatives (e.g. "הוסיפו"), never slash forms. Right-to-left: keep punctuation and any Latin tokens (e.g. "iCloud") correctly placed for RTL. Friendly register; warmth comes from clear, natural phrasing.
locales.hi: Conversational Hindi in Devanagari. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.hr: Second-person plural verb forms, lowercase "vi/vaš". Warmth comes from modern, natural phrasing, not calqued and not informal.
locales.hu: Formal third-person verb forms (e.g. "Adja meg", "költségvetése"), using "Ön" only when a pronoun is unavoidable and never "maga". Warmth comes from modern, plain phrasing, never stiff or bureaucratic register. Hungarian runs long — keep labels tight.
locales.id: Warmth comes from friendly, plain everyday Indonesian as used in popular consumer apps, not slang.
locales.it: Natural, courteous Italian, never slangy; avoid unnecessary anglicisms.
locales.ja: Get warmth through light, soft, approachable phrasing (Apple Japan's voice), not by dropping politeness; avoid stiff keigo. Use katakana for loanwords (e.g. アプリ). The English em-dash habit does not translate — restructure instead.
locales.kn: Natural Kannada in Kannada script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.ko: Plain 반말 reads as wrong, and the stiffer 합니다체 reads distant, so don't drift into it (short button labels can stay noun forms). Warmth comes from clean, light phrasing and natural English loanwords (common in Korean tech), not from dropping politeness. Match Apple Korea's voice.
locales.ml: Natural Malayalam in Malayalam script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.mr: Conversational Marathi in Devanagari. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.ms: Warmth comes from friendly, natural Malay as used in consumer apps, not slang.
locales.or: Natural Odia in Odia script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.pa: Conversational Punjabi in Gurmukhi (Indian Punjabi) script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.pl: Imperatives like "Dodaj", and the courtesy capital "Twój/Twoja" when a possessive is needed. Friendly, natural, not stiff.
locales.pt-BR: Brazilian Portuguese. Warm, not slangy. Brazilian orthography and vocabulary.
locales.pt-PT: European Portuguese; third-person verbs with "o seu/a sua", leaving the pronoun "você" out (it can read curt). Warmth comes from light, direct phrasing, not tutear. European orthography and vocabulary; avoid Brazilian-specific terms.
locales.ro: Modern Romanian; dumneavoastră verb forms, e.g. "Adăugați"; write the pronoun out, not "dvs.", and only when unavoidable. Warmth comes from modern, natural phrasing, not informality.
locales.ru: "вы" (lowercase, as in UI copy). Warmth comes from natural, light, non-calque Russian, not bureaucratic канцелярит.
locales.sk: Vykanie: second-person plural verb forms, lowercase "vy/váš" consistently, never mixing in tykanie. Modern Slovak; warmth comes from natural phrasing, not informality.
locales.sl: Vikanje: second-person plural verb forms, lowercase. Warmth comes from natural, non-calqued phrasing, not tikanje. Note Slovenian's dual number: count-dependent strings need the dual ("two") form, not just one/other.
locales.ta: Natural Tamil in Tamil script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.te: Natural Telugu in Telugu script. The modern feel comes from warmth, brevity, and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.th: Polite, friendly Thai — leave the pronoun out where Thai would, and get politeness from polite phrasing (e.g. โปรด/กรุณา where natural), not from the speaker-gendered particles ครับ/ค่ะ, which UI strings don't use; the modern feel comes from light, contemporary phrasing, not from dropping politeness. Follow normal Thai spacing conventions.
locales.tr: Plural verb forms and suffixes, e.g. "Ekleyin", "bütçeniz"; short button labels may use the bare stem ("Ekle", "Sil") as Turkish UI normally does. Warmth comes from friendly, natural phrasing, not from "sen".
locales.uk: "ви" (lowercase, as in UI copy). Warmth comes from modern, natural phrasing, not calqued from Russian or English.
locales.ur: Conversational Urdu in Nastaliq (Arabic) script. Right-to-left: keep punctuation and any Latin tokens (e.g. "iCloud") correctly placed for RTL. The modern feel comes from warm, light phrasing and natural English loanwords (e.g. "budget"), not informal pronouns.
locales.vi: Leave the pronoun out where Vietnamese would, and never use casual pronouns like "cậu"/"mày" or the service-counter "quý khách". Friendly, natural Vietnamese as used in popular consumer apps.
locales.zh-Hans: Simplified Chinese, mainland China conventions. Concise, modern app tone; avoid Taiwan-specific vocabulary. Mainland copy is punchy and benefit-dense — short rhythms land well, but keep it calm and avoid exclamation-heavy hype.
locales.zh-Hant: Traditional Chinese, Taiwan conventions. Don't drift into "您" (e.g. in error or sync messages). Concise, modern app tone; avoid mainland-specific vocabulary.
